title: GET /me returns passwordHash and resetToken
hint: The page shows a few fields. Look at everything the server actually sent.
explanation: The endpoint serialises the whole database row. The UI ignores the extra fields, but anyone with DevTools sees the password hash and a live password reset token.

title: "Member since January 1970"
hint: Compare the date on the page with createdAt in the response.
explanation: createdAt is a Unix timestamp in seconds, but it is passed to new Date() as milliseconds.

title: Any user can make themselves an admin (mass assignment)
hint: Look at the body of the save request. Then send your own version of it from the Console.
explanation: The client sends role in PUT /me and the server copies every known field from the body, role included. fetch('pulse-api/me', { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ role: 'admin' }) }) is enough.

title: Other users' orders are available by changing the id (IDOR)
hint: There is a user id in one of the request URLs. Whose orders are behind the neighbouring id?
explanation: GET /users/{id}/orders does not check that the id belongs to the current user. /users/1041/orders returns another customer's orders with a shipping address.

title: Order totals are shown in cents: a monthly plan costs 999 €
hint: Would you pay that much for a monthly subscription?
explanation: The API returns amounts in cents (999 = 9.99 €), but the UI prints the raw number with a euro sign.

title: The error response leaks the SQL query and a stack trace
hint: Save an email the server will not like, then read the response, not the message on the page.
explanation: An invalid email returns 400 with a debug object: the raw UPDATE query with your input concatenated into it and server file paths. The UI only shows a generic error, so the leak is visible only in DevTools.

title: "Profile saved" is shown when the server rejected the changes
hint: The bio has a limit. Go over it and check what was really saved.
explanation: A too long bio returns 200 with { ok: false, error }. The client checks only the HTTP status and reports success, while nothing was saved.

title: One click on Save sends two PUT requests
hint: Count the requests in the Network tab after one click.
explanation: The button has an onClick handler that sends the request, and as a submit button it also fires the form's onSubmit, which sends it again.

title: Refresh shows stale data and sends no request
hint: Save a change, then press Refresh and watch both the page and the Network tab.
explanation: GET responses are kept in an in-memory cache that is never invalidated. After a save, Refresh returns the old profile from the cache without calling the API.

title: "Photo removed" although the server answered 500
hint: Remove the photo and check the response status.
explanation: DELETE /me/avatar always fails with 500, but the client ignores the status and hides the photo. It comes back on the next load.

title: The bio field has no label
hint: What is this field called for a screen reader?
explanation: The textarea has only a placeholder. It disappears on input and is not a reliable accessible name.

title: An empty display name is accepted
hint: What does the profile look like without a name?
explanation: Neither the client nor the server checks that the name is not blank, so the profile header ends up empty.
